links.comparator_used: Flesch Reading Ease readability scores and physician review of the instructions
links.outcome: Identification of comprehension barriers in after-discharge instructions for marginalised patient groups
links.effect: Readability scores favoured Claude for simpler language after revisions, but the AI personas still found persistent medical jargon and vague instructions. No numeric effect reported in the abstract.
links.tradeoff: The personas are simulated, so the findings must be validated with real patients.
links.quote: Whilst Claude was preferred for simpler language after revisions, persona reviews revealed persistent medical jargon and vague instructions that could hinder understanding for marginalised groups.

links.outcome: Clinical accuracy and Flesch Reading Ease readability of LLM-generated after-discharge instructions
links.effect: Physician edits improved accuracy but reduced objective readability scores. No numbers given in the abstract.
links.tradeoff: Clinician-led refinements decreased readability, increasing the risk of poorer post-visit patient understanding.
links.quote: Physician edits improved accuracy but paradoxically reduced objective readability scores.
